html:
A slow, sad song style of Cape Verde, sung in Creole to guitar, violin and cavaquinho, which took shape in the 19th century on the islands of Boa Vista and Brava and later in Mindelo.

Its themes are longing, the sea, emigration and departure, the feeling called sodade. The poet Eugenio Tavares wrote many classic mornas in the early 20th century. Cesaria Evora made it known worldwide from the 1990s. UNESCO added morna to its list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2019. Its sound has links to Brazilian and Portuguese song, and to the long emigration it often mourns.
